requirement:
In authored book chapters, a passage opted into citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary` displays its
body as ordinary Markdown prose, with the same left alignment as the
surrounding prose and no opening citation badge or enclosing border.

A small marker in the right gutter identifies the passage's citation-checking
annotations. It does not claim that recorded evidence is current or accepted.
The outermost eligible citation fence has one marker; nested commentary
belongs to its list rather than displaying another marker.

Activating the marker opens the list of resolved citations from the source
passage, including its opening citation, citation-only metadata paragraphs,
and citations within nested commentary. Citations belonging to nested
requirement or example declarations are excluded. Repeated citations appear
once. Project citations link to their declarations; built-in citations retain
their descriptive hover text. The marker is keyboard operable, has an
accessible label, and shows visible keyboard focus. Opening the list does not
hide the passage. Inline citations within explanatory prose retain their
usual rendering.

Rendering does not change the source passage, its discovered references, or
its review inputs. Unfenced citations, citations inside requirement or example
declarations, and utility-only commentary retain their existing rendering.
rationale:
I did not request any implementation source. I judged the two `{test}`-marked tests in `src/lib.rs` against the obligations in `display`, and they cover them. The main test is `reviewed_passages_show_one_gutter_list_and_preserve_prose_and_literal_contexts`. It builds a chapter containing these cases: - an outer `habeas:util` fence that qualifies because it holds other citations - a citation-only metadata paragraph - an inline citation in prose - a nested `::::{cite}` fence - a nested req, example and definition - code-fence and inline-code literals - an escaped citation - a utility-only fence - an unresolved fence - an HTML-literal fence - an unclosed fence - an unfenced citation outside the passage It covers the obligations like this: - **Ordinary prose, no opening badge or border.** - It parses the output with `pulldown_cmark` and asserts `

Nested prose.

`, `

Utility-only.

` and the emphasized ordinary paragraph. - It asserts that `alt="cite rules.other"` is absent from the prose, so the metadata badge is gone. - It asserts that `alt="cite rules.ready"` appears exactly once in the prose, which is the inline citation, so the nested opening badge is gone. - It asserts that the nested fence's raw text is no longer present. - CSS checks require `padding: 0`, `border: 0` and a left margin of `0` on `.habeas-citation-passage`. The margin check handles shorthand forms. - **One right-gutter marker, nested commentary adds none.** - It asserts exactly one `habeas-citation-passage` and one `habeas-citation-list`. - CSS checks require `position: relative` on the passage, `position: absolute` and `right:` with no `left:` on the marker, and a bounded absolute panel. - **List contents.** - It asserts exactly four `
  • ` items: `habeas:util` (the opening citation), `rules.other` (the metadata paragraph), `rules.ready` (the body, the nested fence and the inline citation, listed once) and `rules.term_rule` (the nested definition). - It asserts that `rules.inside` is excluded. That citation sits in the nested req and example and in the escaped, code and literal contexts. - Each name appears exactly once, which covers the dedup obligation. - **Links and hover text.** - It asserts that `rules.other` links to `rules.html#habeas-req-rules.other`. - It asserts that the built-in `habeas-builtin" title=` hover text is kept. - **Accessibility and non-hiding.** - It asserts a `` as a sibling, so opening the list cannot hide it. - It asserts a `:focus-visible` outline rule. - Keyboard operability comes from the native `
    `/`` element, whose presence is asserted. - **Existing rendering retained.** It checks that all of these keep their usual rendering and text: - the unfenced outside citation, with its link and badge - the nested req and example declarations, with their links, aria-labels and detail-page citations - the utility-only fence, which keeps its `habeas-fenced-ref` rendering and builtin badge - the unresolved, HTML-literal, unclosed and code-literal contexts - **Source unchanged.** It asserts that the source file and `text_references` are unchanged after preprocessing. The second test, `citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details`, is also marked for `display`. It covers other container types: req, example, definition, note, cite, impl and test. For a `:::{cite}` container it asserts the following: - Annotations precede the prose. - Non-opening metadata badges are absent from the visible prose. - The opening badge appears once. - The source and the declaration texts are unchanged. The "does not claim evidence is current or accepted" sentence is a non-behavioral statement and needs no test. I found no unacknowledged adequacy gap.

::::{req} citation_review.book_commentary
A closed `:::{cite} full.name` fence in the book, outside a requirement or
example declaration, opts its explanatory passage into citation review.
A passage needs a review when it contains at least one resolved citation
other than `habeas:util`.
The outermost eligible citation fence identifies the passage. Its opening
citation and citations throughout its body belong to one review, including
citations inside nested commentary containers. References inside nested
requirement or example declarations belong to those declarations' assessments.
The review's subject is the enclosing citation fence's outline node, rather
than the whole chapter. Its inputs include the passage and each cited
declaration or built-in text, with the terminology they use. For project
requirements and examples, the reviewer checks that the passage's claims agree
with and are supported by the cited declarations. Contradicting or unsupported
claims produce a negative assessment. Built-in citations retain their
permitted-role and stated-criteria checks under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
These passages use the citation-review storage, freshness checks, selection,
and `author --all` workflow of {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Their identities follow the existing outline-selector rules. Rendering follows
{cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`. Unfenced book citations retain
their existing behavior.
